title: Morrison Formation: Late Jurassic dinosaurs of western North America
summary: The Morrison Formation, Late Jurassic rock across the western United States dated about 163.5–145 million years ago, holds many of North America's best-known dinosaurs: sauropods such as Apatosaurus, Diplodocus and Camarasaurus, plus Stegosaurus, Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus. At Dinosaur National Monument's Carnegie Quarry the beds are a floodplain with rivers, braided streams and small lakes in a warm, humid landscape.

uncertainty.note: NPS gives 163.5 to 145 Ma; Utah Geology gives Kimmeridgian, about 155–148 Ma. The range here is the NPS one; the narrower Utah range lies inside it.

reviewer_note: The formation covers about 1.5 million km², so the pin is only a representative quarry (GeoNames, Dinosaur Quarry). The two NPS pages share a publisher; utahgeology.com is a non-institutional class "other" source. Age sources differ (163.5–145 vs 155–148 Ma).

beats.caption: The Morrison Formation spreads across the western United States, laid down as an alluvial plain of river channels and floodplains.
At Carnegie Quarry the beds hold Apatosaurus, Diplodocus, Camarasaurus, Stegosaurus, Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, in a floodplain with rivers and small lakes.
So many fossils survived that Allosaurus, Apatosaurus, Diplodocus and Stegosaurus are known from the Morrison; the formation is known worldwide for dinosaurs.
